 Sarfaraz Khan breaks silence on dressing room leak allegations, reveals family was deeply affected
 The Mumbai batter has firmly denied leaking any dressing room information from the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy tour of Australia, saying the episode was a difficult time for his entire family.
 By Vishal Jagtap Published - 21 Nov 2026, 04:14 IST 
 3 Min Read
 Sarfaraz Khan breaks silence on dressing room leak allegations, reveals family was deeply affected (Source: Indiancricketteam/IG) Indian batter Sarfaraz Khan has come forward to deny allegations that he passed dressing room information to outside parties during India's 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy campaign in Australia. The claims surfaced against a backdrop of tension within the touring squad, with reports indicating that head coach Gautam Gambhir addressed the players sharply after India fell to defeat in the fourth Test at Melbourne.
 Sarfaraz travelled to Australia as part of the squad for all five Tests but was not included in any playing eleven. He sustained an injury during the tour and headed to the National Cricket Academy for rehabilitation once the series concluded.
 He recalled the shock of the allegations arriving roughly 20 to 25 days after the BGT had ended, describing the moment his flight touched down in India and his phone was immediately flooded with calls and messages.
 "I was hurt. The moment my flight landed, I started getting calls and messages. A lot was written on social media. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy had ended 20-25 days ago. I was hit during the BGT, and I went to NCA for rehab. Suddenly, the news of dressing room leak allegations started circulating. I was wondering whom I should speak to," said Sarfaraz on Baith and Bol with Aakash Chopra.
 Why did Sarfaraz point to his subsequent selection as proof?
 Sarfaraz argued that the selectors' continued faith in him made the allegations implausible. After the BGT, he was called up for the India A side and later named as a replacement for Sai Sudharsan in the Test series against Sri Lanka in 2026, though an injury prevented him from featuring in either match.
 His most recent international outing before that had been at Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai against New Zealand in November 2024.
 Sarfaraz on Gambhir's response to dressing rooml eak row Read More Sarfaraz on Gambhir's response to dressing rooml eak row
 "Whom should I tell? Nothing of this sort happened, and if it were the case, I would not have been selected for the India A team and then for the Sri Lanka series. I don't know who said this. I was feeling bad, and if I was calling someone, my call was not answered. It was a bad time for my family," he added.
 The pressure grew heavy enough that Sarfaraz switched off his phone to manage the volume of unanswered calls and messages. He spoke about the personal cost to those closest to him.
 "My life is full of struggle, and I was ready to face it. I feel bad for my father, mother, wife and brother. Even a small thing turns big on social media. I heard a saying long ago. If you can't spoil someone's work, spoil their name. The work will get spoiled automatically."
 What role did Gautam Gambhir play when the allegations emerged?
 Gambhir contacted Sarfaraz on two separate occasions after the leak claims became public. The coach also reached out to Sarfaraz's father, Naushad Khan, conveying that Sarfaraz should disregard the noise, concentrate on his cricket, and stay away from what Gambhir called useless matters and politics that had nothing to do with him. Gambhir's message reinforced that he regarded Sarfaraz as a quality cricketer whose focus should remain on performing on the field.
 Across six Tests for India, Sarfaraz has scored 371 runs at an average of 37.10, a tally that includes one century and three half-centuries. The identity of whoever originally made the dressing room leak allegations has not been confirmed publicly, and that aspect of the episode remains unresolved.
